glossary.definition: The designated operational role responsible for authoring, reviewing, executing decisions, and archiving records in a defined supplier quality workflow.
Documented information identifying external providers authorized to supply specified parts, materials, or outsourced processes based on verified qualification criteria.
A formal quality record issued to an external provider requiring root-cause investigation, containment, corrective action, and recurrence prevention evidence following a nonconformance.
A governance classification denoting software modules or functions—such as external supplier portals—that are scheduled or under evaluation rather than verified, production-ready capabilities.
Formal authorization granted by an authorized technical authority to accept and use externally provided material or components that do not conform to initial specifications.
A mandatory governance protocol requiring an authorized human owner to evaluate, validate, or reject automated or AI suggestions before commitment into a controlled quality record.
A comparative evaluation record scoring software capabilities against operational workflow requirements, noting whether features are verified with sample data, unverified, or pending release.
An unalterable, automated log of user actions, status modifications, inspection dispositions, and evidence attachment updates that records timestamps and user identities.

A temporary qualification status permitting limited purchase orders under specific constraints, such as calendar expiration or enhanced receiving inspections, while outstanding qualification deliverables remain pending.
A mandatory operational control milestone or sequential sign-off requirement that halts workflow progression until authorized technical, commercial, or quality stakeholders record approval.

example.label: Illustrative example
example.description: An unnamed Canadian industrial machinery manufacturer evaluates supplier quality management software across incoming fabrication, machining, and electronic sub-assemblies. All workflows, audits, and nonconformance records described are illustrative and do not represent actual customer results.

reviewedChapters.title: Mapping the current workflow: Supplier quality management software
reviewedChapters.summary: The guide chapter strictly aligns with the plan and research brief. It defines the operational workflow problem across qualification, receiving inspection, and corrective action handoffs; incorporates practical APG guidance with required disclaimers; notes the pending capability register status for ICC supplier portal functions; satisfies all assigned workflow roles, inputs, decisions, records, and exceptions; labels all hypothetical examples clearly; and excludes unassigned FAQ content.
decisions: Determine whether handoff bottlenecks between purchasing and receiving quality require integrated workflow automation
Verify whether supplier purchase orders contain verified drawing numbers, acceptance standards, and statutory clauses
Authorize or deny placement of external provider on the controlled Approved Supplier List
Assign mandatory receiving inspection levels, sampling protocols, and required Mill Test Report validations

reviewedChapters.title: Evaluating software capabilities: Supplier quality management software
reviewedChapters.summary: The chapter adheres precisely to the plan and source research. It establishes an operational, workflow-based framework for evaluating supplier quality management software across qualification, receiving inspection, and SCAR integration. Core capabilities are clearly distinguished from pending roadmap items, referencing the capability register status on the ICC product page and auditor guidance from the ISO 9001 APG. Each subsection systematically addresses its assigned role, input, decision, record, exception, and evaluation criteria, supplemented by clearly labeled illustrative examples. Unassigned FAQ content is correctly omitted, and all links match approved sources.
decisions: Determine which software vendors meet mandatory operational integration criteria for formal demonstration
Accept, modify, or reject AI-generated nonconformance descriptions and disposition recommendations
Determine if system audit trail meets electronic signature integrity and data tampering prevention standards
Determine whether licensing models align with operational headcount across receiving bays and quality teams

reviewedChapters.title: Qualifying and approving suppliers: Supplier quality management software
reviewedChapters.summary: The chapter adheres precisely to the plan and source research. It establishes an operational, risk-tiered framework for qualifying and approving external providers in supplier quality management software. Risk categorization, certification scope validation, multi-stage approval gates, and conditional approval expiration rules are systematically addressed with corresponding roles, inputs, decisions, records, exceptions, and software evaluation criteria. All hyperlinks match verified source URLs, ISO/IAF APG auditor guidance is properly contextualized with its advisory disclaimer, pending ICC portal capabilities are accurately framed as demonstration evaluation questions, and unassigned FAQ content is correctly omitted.
decisions: Assign provider risk tier and establish mandatory qualification evidence requirements
Evaluate whether certified scope matches contracted manufacturing services
Grant final approval for external provider addition to the active Approved Supplier List
Grant temporary conditional approval limited to a purchase order quantity or calendar window
